name: Gather
tagline: Build a small spatial web room with basic movement and text presence
verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Gather, build a small spatial web room with basic movement and text presence. The hard boundary is real-time spatial media, maps, integrations, moderation, and hosted capacity, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: host a private space for build a small spatial web room with basic movement and text presence, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control
whatYouLose: real-time spatial media, maps, integrations, moderation, and hosted capacity
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Gather because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Gather in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a private space for build a small spatial web room with basic movement and text presence, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
